The prose in regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions ('not FDA regulated, not involving human subjects, de-identified samples') is on its own a record that no restriction applies, but the governance contact and the applying use restriction are constraints.

software_output.evidence: external_resources reference the Cell Mapping Toolkit source repository at https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline and the FAIRSCAPE framework at https://fairscape.github.io; extension_mechanism.contribution_url points at the same repository.

issues_detected.description: Version numbering regresses across the release series: this June 2026 release declares version '2.0', while version_access records the earlier June 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R) and October 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM) as version 2.1, and the citation string ends 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'. A later release carrying a lower version string than its predecessors is not reconcilable as stated.
issues_detected.recommendation: Distinguish the Dataverse per-deposit version (V2) from the CM4AI release-series version, or state explicitly that each quarterly release is a separate Dataverse dataset whose internal version numbers are not comparable across deposits.

issues_detected.description: No software is named for producing or transforming the data actually distributed in this release. The named tooling (node2vec, DenseNet-121, HiDeF, GPT-4/GSAI, cellmaps_pipeline) produces embeddings and cell maps, which known_limitations states are not included ('This is an interim release and does not contain predicted cell maps'); FAIRSCAPE is described as packaging the release into RO-Crate with provenance metadata. The search/quantification software behind the AP-MS and SEC-MS processed tables and the pipeline behind the Perturb-seq atlas are unstated.
issues_detected.recommendation: Name and version the software that produced each distributed processed_data package (e.g., the MS search engine and quantification tool for AP-MS/SEC-MS, and the single-cell alignment/CRISPR-assignment pipeline for the Perturb-seq atlas), using used_software on preprocessing_strategies.

issues_detected.description: No variable-level metadata is provided. `variables` is absent entirely, and no data dictionary is supplied for the distributed processed tables, despite intended_uses claiming AI-ready data suitable for model training.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add variables with identifiers, types and descriptions for the columns of the AP-MS, SEC-MS and Perturb-seq processed packages, or point to the per-package RO-Crate data dictionaries.

issues_detected.description: Distribution formats identify only the container (ZIP) and the metadata serialization (JSON-LD). The scientific file formats inside the archives are not named; raw_data_format is given generically as 'Multi-channel confocal microscopy image files' rather than a standard (e.g., OME-TIFF, mzML, MatrixMarket/h5ad).
issues_detected.recommendation: Specify the per-collection content formats and media types inside each ZIP, with character encoding for text-based tables.

issues_detected.description: No errata and no release-specific change description. updates.update_details states cadence ('quarterly', 'through the end of the project in November 2026') but not what changed in this release relative to the October 2025 release; the only change narrative in the record describes a prior release's revision, carried in related_datasets notes.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add errata or a release-notes entry enumerating what the June 2026 release adds, removes or corrects relative to doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM.

issues_detected.description: Temporal end-of-project statements disagree: collection_timeframes cites NIH RePORTER project period ending 2026-08-31 while updates.update_details and the Dataverse maintenance statement give 'the end of the project in November 2026'. The record itself discloses the discrepancy in source_caveats rather than resolving it.
issues_detected.recommendation: State the project end date used for the maintenance commitment and note that the award period differs, or cite a no-cost-extension end date.

issues_detected.description: No explicit confidentiality_level classification, hipaa_compliant status, or other_compliance framework is recorded; regulatory posture is conveyed only as free text asserting non-applicability, and confidential_elements separately records a pre-publication embargo that is not reflected in a confidentiality level.
issues_detected.recommendation: Set confidentiality_level explicitly and record the embargo status of the Perturb-seq depositions in the regulatory block, not only in confidential_elements.

issues_detected.description: Instance counts for this specific release are deliberately withheld. source_caveats explains that portal-level counts (53,788 images; 7,023 proteins; 21.4 TB) describe the project rather than this release, and the per-condition image count (464 vs 563) is attributed to earlier releases rather than asserted here, so no image count for the June 2026 release exists in the record.
issues_detected.recommendation: Report per-package counts for this release (images per condition, proteins quantified per SEC-MS run, cells and guides in the released Perturb-seq atlas).

issues_detected.description: No download_url slot is populated and no imputation_protocols or missing_data_documentation is present; access is documented only through the landing page and the distribution_formats note describing the 1.9 GB per-file limit and the Dataverse Data Access API.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate download_url with the Dataverse Data Access API endpoint for the persistent ID, and state explicitly that no imputation was performed if that is the case.

semantic_insights: DOI prefix 10.18130 is the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData) prefix and is consistent with page, citation and publisher ROR:0153tk833 (University of Virginia); the id field repeats the same DOI as a CURIE.

Three NIH award numbers parse correctly against NIH conventions: 1OT2OD032742-01 and 3OT2OD032742-01S2 (type 1/3, OT2 other-transaction activity code, OD institute, supplement suffix S2) and 5U54HG012513-02 (type 5, U54 center cooperative agreement, NHGRI), the last matching the Bridge2AI Bridge Center as named.

Cell line RRIDs are well formed Cellosaurus identifiers (RRID:CVCL_0419 for MDA-MB-468, RRID:CVCL_B5P3 for KOLF2.1J) and are attached to the correct lines, giving the subpopulation description resolvable provenance for the biological material.

The non-human-subjects claim is internally coherent across five independent fields: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects=false, direct_collection.is_direct=false, is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present=false, sensitive_elements.sensitive_elements_present=false and at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included=false, each with a stated rationale rather than a bare flag.

Deidentification reasoning is appropriate to the data type: for immortalized and donor-derived cell lines the record argues non-matchability rather than asserting a clinical technique such as Safe Harbor, which would be semantically misapplied here.

Ethical oversight is documented without human subjects, via named ethical review contacts with institutional addresses and a Data Access Committee whose remit (dual licensing, commercialization supervision) is described - the governance structure the record documents is the one its licensing terms actually require.

The licence chain is consistent end to end: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 at dataset level, data_use_permission no_commercial_use, ip_restrictions naming distinct copyright holders per package (UC Regents; Stanford for spatial proteomics images), and an explicit separation of dataset licence from the BSD-3/MIT software licences.

known_biases use enum-aligned categories (selection_bias, sampling_bias) with substantive descriptions, and the selection_bias description is the same statement that sampling_strategies.why_not_representative gives - consistent rather than duplicated boilerplate.

Provenance is layered: was_derived_from at dataset level, raw_data_sources naming four primary modalities with their external repository depositions (MassIVE, SRA/BioProject, Figshare), per-file MD5 checksums, and an RO-Crate metadata package carrying provenance graphs.

The record discloses its own evidentiary limits throughout source_caveats - declining to assert exact byte counts from rounded sizes, declining to carry project-level counts as release values, flagging a disputed author affiliation - which is a documentation strength rather than an omission.

Embargo status is stated where it matters for reuse: external_resources.restrictions flags the Perturb-seq depositions as embargoed and known_limitations tells a user to consult the External Data Links for current availability.

Prefix 10.18130 is the University of Virginia Dataverse registrar prefix, plausible for the stated publisher ROR:0153tk833 (University of Virginia) and the LibraData platform named in third_party_sharing. Prior-release DOIs share the same prefix and V3 shoulder.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description ~1,400 characters enumerating the four modalities, both cell lines, the treatment and differentiation conditions, and the RO-Crate/FAIRSCAPE packaging
sub_elements.quality_note: Well beyond the 200-character threshold and specific rather than generic: it says which modality covers which cell line under which condition, which is the information a user needs to decide relevance.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Description content matches the file_collections manifest (IF images for three MDA-MB-468 conditions, AP-MS treated only, SEC-MS across both lines and derivatives, Perturb-seq atlas plus raw). No modality is described that is absent from the manifest.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability

sub_elements.semantic_validation: Every keyword is instantiated somewhere in the record; no keyword stuffing with unsupported terms. Bridge2AI/CM4AI keywords plus funders establish programme context from quoted values.

sub_elements.evidence: page: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; file_collections: 10 entries each with id, name, path, collection_type, issued date and MD5
sub_elements.quality_note: Landing page is a well-formed Dataverse persistent-ID URL, and the hierarchical resource structure is unusually complete - every distributed archive is itemised with type, date and checksum.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The page URL's persistentId parameter equals the dataset doi. total_file_count: 10 matches the count of file_collections entries exactly.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: 5 typed links - is_new_version_of doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX; is_described_by doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311; is_referenced_by doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734. was_derived_from describes the source experimental interrogation.
sub_elements.quality_note: Relationships are typed and resolvable, with per-link notes explaining what each predecessor release contained; the release series is navigable backwards three quarters.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Predecessor DOIs share the registrant prefix and are cross-checked by version_access.versions_available, which lists the same three DOIs. Preprint DOIs use the 10.1101 bioRxiv prefix correctly.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms spells out CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 clause by clause with data_use_permission: no_commercial_use; ip_restrictions.restrictions: 'Copyright to the data is held by the Regents of the University of California except where otherwise noted; spatial proteomics raw image data is copyright by The Board of Trustees of the Leland Stanford Junior University... The KOLF2.1J iPSC line is available for access by not-for-profit organizations via a simple MTA.'
sub_elements.quality_note: Actionable at the level a reuser needs: it names which institution holds copyright over which package, states the commercial-use negotiation route, and separates the data licence from the BSD-3/MIT software licences.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistent with data_governance.access_review_process, which describes the Data Access Committee supervising 'potential dual licensing for commercial use' - the same restriction expressed from the governance side.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions: 'The release records the dataset as not FDA regulated, not involving human subjects, and comprising de-identified samples.'; regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact: Jillian Parker; data_governance.committee_name 'Data Access Committee', committee_contact 'Jillian Parker', access_review_process described; confidential_elements records a pre-publication embargo
sub_elements.quality_note: The regulatory posture is stated with its basis and a named responsible governance contact is given, which is the sub-element's governance-contact scope. Weakened by the absence of an explicit confidentiality_level, hipaa_compliant status or other_compliance framework, and by the embargo being recorded only in confidential_elements.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The 'no human subjects / de-identified / not FDA regulated' triple is consistent with human_subject_research.regulatory_compliance, which quotes the same release record. Recorded as a low-severity completeness issue rather than a contradiction.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: page: Dataverse persistent-ID landing page; distribution_formats.notes: 'Individual files below the repository's 1.9 GB download limit may be downloaded directly; the dataset as a whole is too large to download as a single ZIP, and the Dataverse Data Access API is offered for programmatic access.'; file_collections give per-archive path and MD5
sub_elements.quality_note: The dedicated download_url slot is empty, but the sub-element also credits platform access instructions, and these are specific and operationally useful - they tell a user the per-file size ceiling, that whole-dataset ZIP download will fail, and which API to use instead, plus the checksums to verify against.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The stated 1.9 GB limit is consistent with the file inventory: the three IF archives (4.6, 4.2, 3.8 GB) exceed it while all others are KB-to-MB scale, so the instruction is not boilerplate but matches this release's actual sizes.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: [{format: ZIP archive, media_type: application/zip}, {format: RO-Crate metadata package, media_type: application/ld+json}]; compression: zip at dataset level and on every file_collection
sub_elements.quality_note: Formats are named with correct MIME types and the RO-Crate entry is tied to the cm4ai_release_metadata.zip collection that carries conforms_to: RO-Crate. Content formats inside the archives are not specified, which is logged as a medium-severity gap under Element 3.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: media_type values are valid registered types and correctly paired with their formats (application/zip for ZIP, application/ld+json for RO-Crate JSON-LD). Dataset-level compression: zip agrees with all ten per-collection compression values.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: 5 typed entries; external_resources: 11 entries covering MassIVE depositions (SEC-MS iPSC, SEC-MS MDA-MB-468, AP-MS paclitaxel, AP-MS vorinostat), NCBI BioProject/SRA with embargo restrictions, Figshare, cm4ai.org, github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline, fairscape.github.io, integrativemodeling.org, ndexbio.org
sub_elements.quality_note: Exceptionally dense linkage: the underlying primary-data depositions are individually enumerated per modality and per treatment arm, and each is flagged archival, with the embargoed one carrying an explicit restriction.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: external_resources depositions correspond one-to-one with raw_data_sources.access_details and with third_party_sharing.notes; no repository is named in one place and contradicted in another.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: distribution_formats populated, page resolves to the Dataverse deposit, licence explicitly permits share and adapt.
sub_elements.evidence: license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Users are free to share... and adapt... under the terms of Attribution... NonCommercial... ShareAlike... and No additional restrictions.'
sub_elements.quality_note: A named, standard, machine-identifiable licence with its permissions and obligations enumerated, plus the citation obligation ('publications referencing this data... should cite the related publication as well as directly citing the data collection'). Reuse conditions are unambiguous.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Licence restrictiveness is proportionate: NC/SA on non-clinical cell-line data with no privacy basis for restriction, consistent with the commercialization-supervision rationale in data_governance.notes rather than with a participant-protection rationale that would be misplaced here.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (see above).
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: ZIP archive / application/zip and RO-Crate metadata package / application/ld+json; file_collections[cm4ai_release_metadata].conforms_to: RO-Crate, conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; per-file MD5 checksums
sub_elements.quality_note: Passes on the strength of RO-Crate/JSON-LD, a genuine community packaging standard with a correct media type, plus checksums enabling integrity verification. It passes marginally: ZIP is a container rather than a data format, character encoding is nowhere stated, and the scientific formats inside the archives (image, mass-spectrometry and single-cell matrix files) are never named, so a reuser cannot tell what they will find on unzipping.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: raw_data_sources.raw_data_format gives only 'Multi-channel confocal microscopy image files', a description rather than a format identifier; no OME-TIFF, mzML, mzTab, MatrixMarket or h5ad is asserted anywhere. Logged as a medium-severity completeness issue.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (see above).
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; file_collections[release-metadata].conforms_to: RO-Crate with conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; instances carry ontology CURIEs B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19/58/59/64 and B2AI_TOPIC:15/26/34
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is stated at three levels - the metadata record's own schema, the packaging standard of the metadata archive, and ontology terms typing each instance's substrate and topic.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: source_caveats is explicit and defensible about scope: conforms_to is asserted only on the RO-Crate-packaged component because the bundle does not state a content standard for the image, MS and sequencing content. Declining to over-assert conformance is the semantically correct behaviour, and the conformance that is asserted is real.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (see above), so variable-level documentation is required for the distributed data.
sub_elements.evidence: No `variables` slot anywhere in the record; is_tabular: false; no data dictionary is referenced for any of the seven processed_data or raw_data archives
sub_elements.quality_note: Fails outright. Nothing in the record describes the fields, columns or channels of the distributed AP-MS, SEC-MS or Perturb-seq packages, so a reuser cannot know what a downloaded table contains without opening it. The per-instance data_substrate/data_topic CURIEs type the modality, not the variables.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Inconsistent with intended_uses, which claim 'AI-ready datasets to support research in functional genomics' and 'AI model training': AI-readiness as the record itself defines it in notes requires data 'fully characterized', which absent variable metadata is not.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: 5 categories with examples (AI-ready research data, model training, biological analysis, perturbation and disease analysis, interpretable ML with usage_notes); prohibited_uses: 'not to be used in clinical decision-making or in any context involving patient care without appropriate regulatory oversight and approval'; discouraged_uses: 2 entries (integrated cell-map analysis premature; use without domain expertise)
sub_elements.quality_note: All three guidance channels are populated with distinct, non-overlapping content, and the discouraged uses are specific to this release's actual state rather than generic caution.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The discouragement against integrated cell-map analysis matches known_limitations ('does not contain predicted cell maps') and anomalies; the prohibition is proportionate to non-clinical cell-line data and is echoed in future_use_impacts as an anticipated misuse. Guidance and limitations tell the same story.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition NOT met (E1 description names cell lines only; E8 collection_mechanisms describe instruments, not recruitment). Governance condition MET on E2 evidence: regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact names Jillian Parker, and license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission=no_commercial_use with ip_restrictions requiring separate commercial licence negotiation is a governance constraint that applies. Scored on the governance disjunct.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries with review_details and contact_person - Vardit Ravitsky (ravitskyv@thehastingscenter.org) and Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon (jean-christophe_belisle-pipon@sfu.ca), the second described as 'working with the project's Ethics module on guidelines, best practices, and governance milestones for ethical AI development on CM4AI data'; human_subject_research.ethics_review_board names the same contacts; data_governance.committee_name 'Data Access Committee' with committee_contact Jillian Parker and a described access_review_process
sub_elements.quality_note: For a dataset with no human participants, this is substantive rather than pro forma: named reviewers with institutional affiliations and reachable addresses, a named governance body with a stated remit (dissemination ethics, dual licensing, commercialization supervision), and a stated rationale for why formal IRB review is not the applicable mechanism. No data protection impact assessment is present, which is proportionate given no personal data.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistency rule 'IF involves_human_subjects=True THEN expect IRB' does not fire - the flag is false. The claimed oversight is plausible for the data type: ethics review of an AI-readiness and dissemination programme rather than of human-subjects protocols. data_governance.source_caveats honestly flags that the release labels the body 'Data Governance Committee' while the preprint calls it 'A Data Access Committee'.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same determination as sub-element 1: human-subjects condition not met on E1/E8 evidence; governance condition met on E2 evidence (governance_committee_contact plus an applying commercial-use restriction). Scored on the governance disjunct.
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false; is_deidentified.deidentification_details: 'CM4AI data are non-clinical, deriving from tissue cultures, and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject. The June 2026 release record states that samples are de-identified and that the dataset does not involve human subjects.'
sub_elements.quality_note: The record states the basis of the de-identification claim rather than asserting a bare flag, and hedges it correctly ('with current knowledge'). It does not name a formal technique, but for immortalised and donor-derived cell lines no identifier-removal method is the operative mechanism - non-derivability is.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Method appropriateness check passes: invoking HIPAA Safe Harbor or k-anonymity here would be a category error, since there is no record-level personal data to transform. Consistent with sensitive_elements.sensitive_elements_present=false and with direct_collection.is_direct=false. The one residual consideration the record leaves unaddressed is donor traceability of the KOLF2.1J line via HipSci, noted but not scored against, as the line is a public resource.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition fails on evidence from other elements: E1 description names 'MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells' and 'KOLF2.1J induced pluripotent stem cells' with no participants, patients or clinical research; E1 keywords contain no participant term; E8 collection_mechanisms describe mass spectrometry, confocal microscopy, 10x Genomics kits and a pipetting robot, with no recruitment; E8 direct_collection.is_direct=false states 'Data were not collected from individuals.' The governance disjunct does not reach sub-elements 3-5: a Data Access Committee and a commercial-use restriction are not a participant signal.
sub_elements.evidence: No participants exist to protect; participant_privacy and reidentification_risk are absent, and the exclusion rests on E1/E8 evidence rather than on that absence.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. Scoring 0 here would measure the dataset's subject matter - cell lines rather than people - instead of its documentation quality.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same E1/E8 evidence as sub-element 3: no human participants are described or recruited; all material derives from established cell lines available from ATCC and the HipSci resource (direct_collection.collection_details). The governance disjunct does not reach this sub-element.
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent is absent; there is no participant from whom consent could be obtained for this release.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. Donor consent for the originating KOLF2.1J and MDA-MB-468 lines is upstream of this dataset and is handled by the cell-line resources, which the record identifies by RRID and describes as 'ethically sourced'.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same E1/E8 evidence as sub-elements 3 and 4: no human participants. Note that at_risk_populations IS populated in this record (at_risk_groups_included: false), but applicability is determined from E1/E8 evidence and not from Element 4's own fields, and there are no participants who could be at risk or compensated.
sub_elements.evidence: at_risk_populations.notes: 'all data derive from established human cell lines rather than from living individuals, so no at-risk population protections apply'; participant_compensation absent.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. The record's own negative declaration is good documentation practice, but there is no participant population for the sub-element to assess.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: subpopulations[0]: subpopulation_elements_present: true; identification names both lines and all five conditions (MDA-MB-468 untreated/DMSO, paclitaxel, vorinostat; KOLF2.1J parental, NPC, neuron, cardiomyocyte); distribution gives per-condition IF archive sizes; notes give donor provenance - 'MDA-MB-468 (RRID:CVCL_0419) was established from a metastatic site pleural effusion of a 51-year-old black female'; 'KOLF2.1J (RRID:CVCL_B5P3) was derived from a healthy male Northern European donor.'
sub_elements.quality_note: The biological analogue of cohort characterisation is done properly: the strata are named, the donor characteristics behind each line are given, and the distribution field states honestly where per-stratum counts are not uniform across modalities.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Both RRIDs are well-formed Cellosaurus identifiers and correctly paired with their lines. The donor descriptions are the standard published provenance for these lines and are internally consistent with the selection_bias statement in known_biases.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: total_file_count: 10 with per-archive sizes (4.6, 4.2, 3.8 GB; 113.3, 135.8, 171.8, 93.9, 30.2, 73.3 KB; 1.1 MB); instances notes give '11,739 targeted genes' for the KOLF2.1J atlas, 'approximately 7,000 proteins' for SEC-MS, '464 proteins of interest per condition' (attributed to the June 2025 release); acquisition_methods report 'Seventeen genes were endogenously tagged in MDA-MB-468', '72 of 100 chromatin modifiers', 'more than 700 protein complexes'

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (see above).
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: five entries each with an explicit relationship_type - is_new_version_of (three prior quarterly releases, by DOI), is_described_by (doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311, the CM4AI preprint), is_referenced_by (doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734, the Perturbation Cell Atlas preprint) - with per-entry notes explaining the target
sub_elements.quality_note: Relationship types are drawn from standard vocabulary, applied correctly, and every target is a resolvable DOI with an explanatory note; the release series and its describing literature are both navigable.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: is_described_by is correctly reserved for the preprint that describes this dataset, while the Perturbation Atlas paper is is_referenced_by - the distinction is applied with care rather than using one predicate for all links. Targets agree with version_access and with source_caveats' statement that the Nature U2OS paper is deliberately not claimed as a CM4AI release.

strengths: Provenance and identifier hygiene are exemplary: a consistent Dataverse DOI across id, doi, citation, page and version_access; three parseable NIH award numbers; ~40 creators with ORCIDs and role annotations; ROR for the publisher; Cellosaurus RRIDs for both cell lines; and per-file MD5 checksums for all ten archives.

Ethical documentation is proportionate and complete for a non-human-subjects dataset: named ethics contacts with reachable addresses, a Data Access Committee with a stated remit over dual licensing and commercialization, and a de-identification claim argued from non-derivability rather than borrowing a clinical technique that would not apply.

Access and licensing are unambiguous down to the package level: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with clause-by-clause terms, per-package copyright attribution (UC Regents generally, Stanford for the spatial proteomics images), the commercial-use negotiation route, and an explicit separation of data licence from the BSD-3/MIT software licences.

Technical method documentation is dense and quantitative - four acquisition modalities with library design, tagging counts and yield figures; four collection mechanisms with per-channel marker assignments; and a five-step preprocessing pipeline with a named annotation protocol including confidence scoring.

Limitations, biases and anomalies are release-specific, typed and mutually corroborating: the absent cell maps, the embargoed depositions and the incomplete cross-modality protein overlap each appear in several fields with a consistent story, and two limitations carry impact or mitigation statements.

The record models honest evidentiary discipline: source_caveats declines to convert rounded file sizes into byte counts, refuses to carry project-level counts as release figures, attributes a changed per-condition image count to the release that stated it, and discloses a conflicting author affiliation instead of silently choosing one.

Ecosystem integration is thorough - four separate MassIVE depositions enumerated per modality and treatment arm, SRA and Figshare links with embargo flags, NDEx for map sharing, a documented toolkit repository with readthedocs, and five typed related-dataset relationships spanning three prior releases and two describing preprints.
weaknesses: No software is named for producing or transforming the data actually distributed: the well-documented tooling (node2vec, DenseNet-121, HiDeF, GPT-4/GSAI, cellmaps_pipeline) produces cell maps the record states are not in this release, and FAIRSCAPE only packages it, leaving the MS search and single-cell processing software behind the seven processed archives unstated.

Variable-level metadata is entirely absent - no `variables`, no data dictionary, no column or channel definitions - which is in tension with the record's own AI-ready and model-training claims and costs points in both Element 3 and Element 5.

Only container formats are specified: ZIP and RO-Crate/JSON-LD are named with correct media types, but the scientific formats inside the archives and the character encoding of text tables are never stated, so a user cannot anticipate what unzipping yields.

There is no errata and no release-specific change description; updates.update_details carries cadence rather than change content, and the only change narrative in the record belongs to a predecessor release, so a user cannot tell what June 2026 adds relative to October 2025.

The version string regresses across the series - '2.0' here against '2.1' recorded for both the June 2025 and October 2025 predecessors - and this is left unreconciled, which undermines the otherwise strong version-access documentation.

Release-level instance counts are not asserted for any modality, so the number of images, proteins or cells in this particular release cannot be determined from the record even though nearby counts for the project and for other releases are supplied.

Missing-data handling is undocumented across all modalities: no missing_data_documentation and no imputation_protocols, not even a statement that imputation was not performed, which matters for the mass-spectrometry packages.

Regulatory metadata is free text without structured classification - no confidentiality_level, hipaa_compliant or other_compliance - and the pre-publication embargo that genuinely constrains access is recorded only in confidential_elements rather than in the regulatory block.
recommendations: Attach used_software, with names and versions, to the preprocessing_strategies for each distributed package - the MS search engine and quantification tool behind the AP-MS and SEC-MS elution profiles, and the alignment and guide-assignment pipeline behind the Perturb-seq atlas - so a reader can tell what produced the released data rather than the not-yet-released cell maps.

Add a `variables` block with identifiers, types, units and descriptions for the columns of each processed package, or reference the per-package RO-Crate data dictionaries from the dataset-level record.

Specify the content formats and media types inside each ZIP (e.g. OME-TIFF or the actual image format for the IF archives, mzML/mzTab for the MS packages, the matrix format for the Perturb-seq atlas) together with character encoding for text-based tables.

Add an errata or release-notes entry enumerating what the June 2026 release adds, corrects or removes relative to doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, and reconcile the version string - either explain that Dataverse per-deposit versions are not comparable across the release series, or renumber so that later releases carry higher versions.

Report per-release instance counts for each modality (images per condition, proteins quantified per SEC-MS run, cells and guides in the released atlas), keeping the existing practice of attributing project-level figures separately.

Populate download_url with the Dataverse Data Access API endpoint for the persistent ID, and record the embargo in the regulatory block alongside an explicit confidentiality_level, so access constraints are discoverable from the compliance metadata and not only from confidential_elements.
Document missing-data handling: add missing_data_documentation for the MS and single-cell packages and an imputation_protocols entry, stating explicitly if no imputation was performed.

Consider recording a conflict-of-interest statement in ethical_reviews and adding split or subset typing (is_data_split, is_subpopulation) so that the cell line x condition structure already described in prose becomes machine-readable.
